title: I Dreamed That You Were Taking Me
text:
I dreamed that you were taking me

along a white path,

through the green countryside,

toward the blue of the sierras,

toward the blue mountains,

on a serene morning.


I felt your hand in mine,

your companion's hand,

your child's voice in my ear

like a new bell,

like a virgin bell

of a spring dawn.


They were your voice and your hand,

in dreams, so true!...


Live, hope, who knows

what the earth swallows!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dream-walk, companion hand, and final appeal to hope.

title: Beloved, the Breeze Says...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the refrain of unseen beloved and waiting heart as the scene turns funerary.

title: When My Life Is
text:
When my life is,

all clear and light

like a good river

that runs joyfully

to the sea,

to the unknown sea

that waits

full of sun and song.


And when spring bursts

in my heart

you will be, my life,

the inspiration

of my new poem.


A song of peace and love

to the rhythm of the blood

that runs through the veins.

A song of love and peace.

Only of sweet things and words.


Meanwhile,

meanwhile, keep the golden key

of my verses

among your jewels.

Keep it and wait.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the river-to-sea future and the golden key entrusted to the beloved.

title: You Will See the Wonder of the Road
text:
You will see the wonder of the road,

road of dreamed Compostela

—oh lilac and tawny mountain!— pilgrim,

on a plain, among candle poplars.

Autumn with two rivers has gilded

the enclosure of the giant sentinel

of stone and light, towered prodigy

that takes shape in the spotless blue.

You will see on the plain a pack

of keen greyhounds and a hunting lord,

riding toward a distant range,

vain phantom of an old race.

You must enter when in the cold afternoon

a balcony shines in the deserted square.




1925
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Compostela road, towered sentinel, hunting phantom, and cold shining balcony.

title: Did I Pawn Your Memory? How Many Times!
text:
Did I pawn your memory? How many times!

Life descends like a wide river,

and when it carries a tall ship to sea

it goes with greenish silt and murky dregs.


And more if there was storm on its banks,

and it drags the storm's booty,

if in its sky the ashen cloud

caught fire with yellow sparks.


But although it flows toward the unknown sea,

life is also water from a spring

that from a clear source, drop by drop,


or a noisy plume of torrent,

under the blue, over the stone, breaks forth.

And there your name sounds, eternally!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the life-as-river contrast between muddy descent and clear spring.
